prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the vertical layout from the camera wearer looking downward past an open upper cabinet door on the right (0.1 to 0.5 metres away) and interior cabinet shelves on the left (0.3 to 0.8 metres away) toward the kitchen floor and work lights roughly 1.5 to 2.0 metres below. Across frames 1 to 4, the camera wearer's left hand on the lower cabinet hinge, right hand holding a screwdriver about 0.1 metres below the left hand, and lower legs/feet on the floor remain at steady distances, while in frame 5 the camera turns and shifts closer to the right so the bright cabinet door fills the foreground at 0.1 to 0.3 metres and occludes the hands and interior shelves. No other people are present, and the cabinet door, hinges, and screwdriver are all within immediate arm's reach of the camera wearer. The map clearly shows the continuous distance gradient along the angled cabinet door and recessed shelving that is harder to gauge in the flat lighting of the RGB image. However, it is unreliable where the upper cabinet hinge and door edge are assigned brighter values (appearing nearer) than the hands and screwdriver directly below them, and where bright floor work lights cause dark drop-offs in the background.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's outstretched arms, hands, and lower legs in the bottom centre of frames 1 to 4, located roughly 0.4 to 0.6 metres (arms) and 1.5 to 1.8 metres (feet) below the camera, while leaving the surrounding cabinet, screwdriver, hinges, and kitchen floor unsegmented in black. Across frames 1 to 4, the left arm extends from the bottom-right toward the centre hinge and the right hand remains just below and to the left holding the screwdriver within arm's reach, before both arms drop completely out of view behind the cabinet door in frame 5 as the camera shifts right. No other people are in the scene; the camera wearer's torso is out of the field of view and their legs are partly occluded by the forearms and screwdriver. This map helps separate the camera wearer's foreground limbs from the busy floor background below, which visually blends together in the RGB strip. It is unreliable because it fails to segment any environmental objects or tools (such as the cabinet, screwdriver, or oven), merges the screwdriver handle and feet into the 'person' mask in frame 1, splits the camera wearer's own left and right limbs into two separate 'person' instances in frame 3, and misses the visible foot at the bottom of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders a miniature full-body yellow skeleton in the lower-left to lower-centre of frames 1 to 4 (and magenta hand keypoints in frame 2) where the camera wearer's own hands, screwdriver, and distant feet overlap in the 2D projection, while frame 5 is completely empty. In reality, only the camera wearer is present, looking downward with both hands within 0.4 to 0.6 metres reaching the lower cabinet hinge and a screwdriver, and feet standing on the floor about 1.5 to 1.8 metres below. Across frames 1 to 4, the plotted skeleton shifts slightly right and tilts further leftward as the camera wearer adjusts their grip and head angle, before disappearing in frame 5 when the cabinet door occludes the limbs. While the magenta keypoints in frame 2 roughly indicate the location of the camera wearer's fingers around the hinge and screwdriver tip, the pose map adds almost no valid spatial information beyond the RGB view. The map is highly unreliable under this extreme downward egocentric viewpoint, hallucinating a miniature full-body torso, head, and legs out of the camera wearer's forearms, screwdriver shaft, and feet, and failing to track the hands altogether in frames 1, 3, and 4.
